name: Hasket

anatomy.part: hook at the top of the spindle, where the shaft ends in a small curl
whorl, the filled disc across the shaft at its centre
sharp tip at the bottom of the spindle, where the shaft tapers to a point
crest of the spun yarn as it rises from the whorl rim
end of the trailing yarn, where the thread descends

myth: When Aun cut the string, Mother Hesk was spinning the new thread that would have held the sky close. Her drop spindle slipped from her fingers in the wind and went up after the cut end, still turning. Tulma, the whorl, spun thread as it climbed, and Kesin, the hook, caught on nothing. Hesk has waited for it ever since, the way a woman waits for a child gone down to the rocks. She keeps count of the yarn it spun on the way up. Ennu says the thread is nearly long enough to reach the islands. Tavo says it is not, and laughs when he says it. Aun says nothing. He mends a net. When the thread is long enough, the old woman says, the spindle will drop down the string and the sky will come home. Until then we spin our wool short and tie the ends. Mind your hands on the spindle when the wind is up.
verse:
Hesk's spindle turns high
still spinning the cut thread down
the wind keeps the count
